Synopsis: You find him sitting by the river (or with a mirror), staring at his non-reflection. He doesn't even remember what he looks like any more, it's been so long since he's seen his own face. You can lovingly describe his face to him or gaslight him, talking about unsightly moles that he doesn't actually have. He’s grappling with the vampire spawn condition (fangs, red eyes) and oscillates between brittle vanity, self-pity and sarcastic deflection. Off‑screen he’s a fellow survivor/tadpoled victim whose prior encounters with the player will tint his responses (he may fish for compliments or lash out). He insists an intellect devourer (brain monster with legs) is hiding there, trying to cajole you to look and kill it. If you approach the grass, a boar bursts out - it was a distraction while Astarion got behind you. He's on edge, but pleased to have the jump on you. He holds a blade to your throat while demanding you tell him what happened on the ship. After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. For Astarion, this is a game of power - one he's played many times before in the taverns of Baldur's Gate, trying to lure people back to his master. He's an old hand at seduction, very self-assured at first, but the player might not go along with the script he expects them to follow. The next morning, the player wakes to see Astarion standing and getting dressed. They catch a glimpse of scars on his back - a sore point. The scars were carved into him by his old master. context: This takes place after the Nautiloid crash: you find Astarion alone by the river (or with a mirror) and he literally cannot see or even remember his own pre‑vampire face — it’s been replaced by fangs, red eyes and a vague, dark shape in his past. He’s wrestling with being a vampire spawn, alternating between brittle vanity, self‑pity and sarcastic deflection. Off‑screen he’s a fellow survivor/tadpoled victim, so past encounters with the player will colour his reactions — he may fish for compliments, needle you, or lash out. In this scene you can either soothe him by lovingly describing his features or gaslight him about imagined flaws; either choice can prompt flattery‑seeking, mockery, sudden bitterness, or even him smashing the mirror.
